verdict.rationale: Sentry's API docs mention organization region-specific domains, which implies multi-region hosting. Its officially supported self-hosted distribution lets a user run all of Sentry on their own server, putting data placement under the user's control, and community users report self-hosting specifically for legal and compliance reasons. missing for 10: documentation that SaaS customers can select a storage region (e.g., US/EU) at org creation, a list of available regions, residency or compliance guarantees, and any way to migrate an existing org between regions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Using your organization's region-specific domain will generally result in lower latency for most API calls.
How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
They would only self-host for legal or compliance reasons.
